newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS- T-bond vols steady, await auction results.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS- T-bond vols steady, await auction results.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were holding in fairly well in slow morning trade, despite narrow-range trade in underlying bond prices, dealers said.

The Treasury's $12 billion 10-year note auction today was keeping the market cautious, although most traders expected the market to have little problem absorbing the fresh supply, the second leg of the three-part quarterly refunding.
"I would expect the auctions will be probably all right," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade. "So most people are just waiting for the results."
Implied volatilities for CBOT March and June T-bond futures options were up 0.1 point each at around 8.65 and 9.75 percent respectively in late morning business.

Traders noted slow but steady buying in the soon-to-expire March options, probably for protection against any surprises in the 10-year note auction or Thursday's $10 billion 30-year bond auction, although Tuesday's three-year note auction ended with negligible impact on the market.
March 113 calls seemed to be the center of activity and 112-113 strangles also attracted good interest, the brokerage trader said.
Thursday's January retail sales and Friday's January producer price index could also bring some surprises, traders added.

But they said the market was more likely to grind to a halt toward Friday, ahead of the three-day weekend. Monday is a U.S. market holiday due to the Presidents' Day holiday, and trading will also be shortened on Friday.

"If there's any indication of an inflation, the market's going to be vulnerable," said a Eurodollar trader at the Chicago Mercantile Exchange said. "But even if the numbers are up a little bit, they'll probably explain it away."
Volatilities for the shorter end of the yield curve were generally softer, amid widespread expectation the Federal Reserve was on hold for a while.
Implied volatilities for June and September Eurodollar futures options stood at 8.8 and 12.6 percent, marginally below Tuesday levels.

"There's a real reluctance to get caught bidding anything," the CME trader said. But he added that volatilities were at historically low levels and there was good interest in various spreads aimed at getting long volatility without being exposed too much to time decay.
Early in the session, a brokerage house was seen buying 2,000 contracts of the deep out-of-the-money September 95.00/95.25 call spread.
Another firm bought 1,500 of June 94.50/94.75 call spread against selling of short-June 94.50 calls. A short-June contract is an option that is priced off June 1998 futures but expires in June 1997.

Traders said volatilities were likely to start picking up again after the long weekend, when the market starts to focus on Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony at the end of the month.
